proofs.full_local_argument: Write V as defined in the statement. The assumed Bregman bound implies convexity and strong convexity of omega on Z. The prox objectives are continuous on compact Z and strongly convex, so their minimizers exist and are unique. For p=argmin_{v∈Z}{<q,v>+V(v,z)}, directional optimality along each segment to u∈Z gives <q+grad omega(p)-grad omega(z),u-p>≥0. Expanding V yields <q,p-u>≤V(u,z)-V(u,p)-V(p,z). Fix one iteration with z=z_{t-1}, w=w_t and p=z_t. Applying this inequality to the corrector (q=gamma F(w)) gives gamma<F(w),p-u>≤V(u,z)-V(u,p)-V(p,z). Applying it to the predictor (q=gamma F(z)) with test point p gives gamma<F(z),w-p>≤V(p,z)-V(p,w)-V(w,z). Add these two inequalities and add gamma<F(w)-F(z),w-p> to obtain gamma<F(w),w-u>≤V(u,z)-V(u,p)-V(p,w)-V(w,z)+gamma<F(w)-F(z),w-p>. Put a=||w-z|| and b=||w-p||. By the dual norm inequality, Lipschitz continuity and strong convexity, the last three terms are at most gamma L a b-(alpha/2)(a²+b²). Since 2ab≤a²+b² and gamma L≤alpha/sqrt(2)≤alpha, this quantity is nonpositive. Thus for every u∈Z, gamma<F(w_t),w_t-u>≤V(u,z_{t-1})-V(u,z_t). Summing for t=1,...,T and using V(u,z_T)≥0 gives gamma sum_t<F(w_t),w_t-u>≤V(u,z0)≤Theta(z0). Monotonicity gives <F(u),w_t-u>≤<F(w_t),w_t-u>. Divide the sum by gamma T and maximize over u∈Z to obtain the weak gap bound. For the saddle conclusion, write w_t=(a_t,b_t). Convexity in x and concavity in y imply, for every (x,y)∈X×Y, f(a_t,y)-f(x,b_t)≤<grad_x f(a_t,b_t),a_t-x>+<grad_y f(a_t,b_t),y-b_t>=<F(w_t),w_t-(x,y)>. Jensen's inequality in each variable gives f(wbar_{T,x},y)-f(x,wbar_{T,y})≤T^{-1}sum_t[f(a_t,y)-f(x,b_t)]≤Theta(z0)/(gamma T). Maximizing independently over x,y yields the claimed full saddle gap; no minimax theorem or substitution of corrected iterates is needed. All averages are feasible by convexity. Finally, if z0 minimizes omega, directional optimality gives <grad omega(z0),u-z0>≥0 for every u∈Z, hence V(u,z0)≤omega(u)-omega(z0) and the stated range bound for Theta. Substituting gamma=alpha/(sqrt(2)L) gives the displayed constant. No termination check is needed: at an exact fixed point the same inequalities remain valid.

assumptions: For all z,v∈Z, <F(z)-F(v),z-v>≥0 and ||F(z)-F(v)||*≤L||z-v|| with a finite L>0.

omega is differentiable on Z with a well-defined gradient and satisfies V(u,z)≥(alpha/2)||u-z||² for all u,z∈Z, alpha>0. Exact minimizers of both displayed prox problems are used. No Lipschitz-gradient assumption on omega is imposed.

For the additional saddle-point conclusion only: E=E_x×E_y, Z=X×Y with nonempty convex compact X,Y; f:X×Y→R is differentiable, convex in x and concave in y, and F(x,y)=(grad_x f(x,y),-grad_y f(x,y)) satisfies the same monotonicity and Lipschitz assumptions.
statement.conclusion: max_{u∈Z}<F(u),wbar_T-u>≤Theta(z0)/(gamma T). Under the additional saddle assumptions, max_{y∈Y}f(wbar_{T,x},y)-min_{x∈X}f(x,wbar_{T,y})≤Theta(z0)/(gamma T). At gamma=alpha/(sqrt(2)L), each bound is sqrt(2)L Theta(z0)/(alpha T). If z0 minimizes omega, Theta(z0)≤max_Z omega-min_Z omega.
statement.objects_and_definitions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with any norm ||·|| and its dual ||·||*. Z⊂E is nonempty convex compact. V(u,z)=omega(u)-omega(z)-<grad omega(z),u-z>; Theta(z0)=max_{u∈Z}V(u,z0). For any z0∈Z and constant gamma, define w_t=argmin_{v∈Z}{gamma<F(z_{t-1}),v>+V(v,z_{t-1})}, z_t=argmin_{v∈Z}{gamma<F(w_t),v>+V(v,z_{t-1})}, and wbar_T=T^{-1}sum_{t=1}^T w_t.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every E,Z,F,omega,alpha,L satisfying the assumptions, every z0∈Z, every fixed gamma in the stated range, and every integer T≥1, the deterministic conclusions hold. The Algorithm selects z0 minimizing omega, but the bound does not require that selection. There is no probabilistic qualification.
